faq.q: How long does a garage door typically last?
faq.a: Most garage doors last 15–30 years, depending on the material, how often you use it and how well it’s maintained. Springs usually wear out much sooner, often after about 10,000 cycles, which works out to 7–10 years for many households.

faq.q: What are signs my garage door needs repair?
faq.a: Watch for grinding or squeaking, jerky or uneven movement, a door that reverses or won’t close all the way, visible gaps or sagging, frayed cables, or an opener that runs while the door doesn’t move. A loud bang from the garage often means a spring has broken.

faq.q: How much do garage door services cost?
faq.a: Cost depends on the type of service, the door’s size and material, the parts needed and where you live. Routine maintenance and small repairs cost much less than replacing springs, installing an opener or putting in a new door.

faq.q: Can I use my garage door if a spring is broken?
faq.a: No. With a broken spring, the door can be extremely heavy and may fall without warning. Don’t try to open it by hand or with the opener. Leave it in place and call a professional.

faq.q: How often should I have my septic tank pumped?
faq.a: Most septic tanks should be pumped every 3–5 years, depending on the size of the tank, the number of people in the household, and water usage. Regular pumping helps prevent backups, odors, and costly system failures.

faq.q: What are the signs that my septic system needs service?
faq.a: Common warning signs include slow drains, sewage backups, foul odors near the tank or drain field, standing water in the yard, and unusually lush grass over the septic area. If you notice any of these issues, it’s important to schedule an inspection promptly.

faq.q: How much does septic tank service cost?
faq.a: The cost varies based on the type of service needed, the size of the tank, and your location. Routine pumping is generally more affordable than major repairs or system replacements. We can connect you with local professionals for a free estimate.

faq.q: Can I use my plumbing while my septic tank is being serviced?
faq.a: In most cases, it’s best to limit water use during septic pumping or repairs. Your technician will let you know if any temporary restrictions are necessary to ensure the service is completed safely and efficiently.
